name: Proxmox Extended Tools
description: Extended Proxmox tools for storage, snapshots, and capacity management

tools.name: Storage Usage
tools.description: Get storage utilization across all Proxmox datastores

warn_percent.description: Percent usage to flag as warning

instructions.summary: Check Proxmox storage capacity across all datastores

tools.name: List Snapshots
tools.description: List all VM/container snapshots with age and size

vmid.description: Filter by VM ID (omit for all)

older_than_days.description: Only show snapshots older than X days

instructions.summary: List snapshots to identify old ones for cleanup

tools.name: Cleanup Snapshots
tools.description: Delete snapshots older than specified age

older_than_days.description: Delete snapshots older than X days

exclude_vmids.description: VM IDs to exclude from cleanup

instructions.summary: Clean up old snapshots to free storage
when_to_use: User wants to clean up old snapshots

tools.name: VM Resource Usage
tools.description: Get detailed CPU, memory, and disk I/O per VM

vmid.description: Specific VM ID (omit for top consumers)

instructions.summary: Check which VMs are using the most resources

tools.name: Node Resources
tools.description: Get CPU, memory, and storage usage for a specific Proxmox node — for capacity planning before placing a new VM, distinct from proxmox.vm.resources (per-VM, not per-node)

instructions.summary: Get resource utilization for a Proxmox node
when_to_use: Planning VM placement — which node has room for a new VM

tools.name: Backup Status
tools.description: Check Proxmox backup job status and recent backups

days.description: Show backups from last X days

tools.name: HA Status
tools.description: Check High Availability cluster status and failover readiness

tools.name: Clone VM
tools.description: Clone a new VM FROM an existing golden template. Quox never creates templates — the source must already be flagged template:1 in Proxmox (see proxmox.templates.list). Approval-gated: creates real infrastructure.

template_vmid.description: Source template VM ID (must be flagged template:1 in Proxmox — get this from proxmox.templates.list)

newid.description: New VM ID for the clone

node.description: Target node (omit for same node as the template)

storage.description: Target storage pool for the clone (omit to use the template's storage)

full.description: Full clone (true, independent disk) or linked clone (false, depends on the template)

instructions.summary: Provision a new VM by cloning an existing golden template
when_to_use: User wants to clone a VM from a template
Creating a new environment from an approved template
when_not_to_use: Source VM is not flagged as a template (check with proxmox.templates.list first)

tools.name: Create Snapshot
tools.description: Create a point-in-time snapshot of an existing virtual machine. Approval-gated: modifies infrastructure state.

instructions.summary: Create a restore point before making changes to a VM
when_not_to_use: VM has insufficient disk space for snapshot

tools.name: VM Pool Status
tools.description: Show the org's disposable test-VM pool: settings, counts by state and every pool VM with its lessee and lease expiry

instructions.summary: See which disposable test VMs are warm, leased or failed
when_to_use: User asks what test VMs are available
Before leasing or releasing a pool VM

tools.name: Lease Pool VM
tools.description: Lease a disposable Ubuntu test VM from the pool (warm if one fits, else built to order). The lessee supplies their own SSH public key; only its fingerprint is stored. Every host command underneath is governed by the org's standing grant or approval.

ssh_pubkey.description: One ssh-ed25519, ssh-rsa or ecdsa public key line

memory_gb.description: RAM in GB (pool default if omitted)

instructions.summary: Hand a throwaway test VM to a session
when_to_use: A session needs a disposable VM to test on

tools.name: Release Pool VM
tools.description: Stop and destroy a pool VM, then re-warm the pool. Only VMs inside the org's configured pool range are touched.

when_to_use: The lessee is done with the VM

tools.name: Configure VM Pool
tools.description: Change the org's VM pool settings (admin settings write, held for approval)

enabled.description: Turn the pool on or off

lanes.description: Placement lanes, each covered by its own standing grant: [{ node, template_vmid, max, clone_mode: linked|full }]

deny_nodes.description: Hard denylist: nodes the pool never places on or touches

prom_url.description: Prometheus base URL for free-RAM-fraction placement (omit to use fewest pool VMs)

backup_window.description: HH:MM-HH:MM UTC during which the scheduler does not warm

vmid_min.description: First VMID the pool may use

vmid_max.description: Last VMID the pool may use

instructions.summary: Adjust the disposable VM pool settings
when_to_use: An admin asks to resize, enable or move the pool

tools.name: Rehearse On Twin
tools.description: Rehearse a command on a disposable, network-isolated twin of a VM (snapshot, full clone with every NIC link_down, health checks before/after) and return a pass/fail verdict plus a rehearsal_id for the approval card

node.description: Proxmox node the target is on

command.description: Shell command to run inside the twin (no single quotes)

keep_twin.description: Leave the stopped isolated twin in place

instructions.summary: Prove a risky change on a throwaway copy before asking a human to approve it
when_to_use: Before proposing a package upgrade, config change or restart on a production VM
A human asks whether a change is safe

tools.name: VM Doctor
tools.description: Diagnose why a VM is slow or unhealthy (read-only): gathers VM status, config, snapshots, hour/day performance history, host node load, storage use, recent tasks and the guest agent, runs fixed rules and returns a verdict with ranked findings (evidence and suggested fix) plus gaps for anything it could not read

instructions.summary: Explain why a VM is slow or unhealthy, with evidence, without touching it
when_to_use: A human asks why a VM is slow, unresponsive or unhealthy
Before proposing a fix, to find the likely cause
